name: STM32WB09KEV6TR
title: Cortex-M0+ wireless MCU with Bluetooth LE 5.4 and 2.4 GHz radio, 512 KB flash
summary: The STM32WB09xE pairs a 64 MHz Cortex-M0+ with a Bluetooth LE 5.4 and proprietary 2.4 GHz radio, 512 KB of flash and 64 KB of SRAM. An on-chip step-down converter, integrated balun and trimmed 32 MHz crystal oscillator keep the outside parts few. It runs from 1.7 V to 3.6 V, draws 12 nA in Shutdown and under 1 µA in Deepstop with RAM kept, and comes in VFQFPN32 (STM32WB09KE) or WLCSP36 (STM32WB09TE), both with 20 GPIOs.
key_figures: -97 dBm at 1 Mbit/s, -104 dBm LE coded S=8

notes: Code: STM32 WB 09, then K (32 pins) or T (36 pins), E (512 Kbytes flash), V (VFQFPN) or F (WLCSP), 6 (-40 °C to +85 °C) or 7 (-40 °C to +105 °C), TR (tape and reel). Packages are ECOPACK2.

circuits.title: Application circuit, DC-DC converter, WLCSP36
circuits.description: Complete minimum system for the WLCSP36 part with the step-down converter running. VDDSD, VDD2 and VDDRF sit on the one VDD supply with two decoupling capacitors each. VLXSD drives the converter inductor L1, then the filter inductor L2, into the output node, which carries C8 and C9 and is fed back into VFBSD. C7 holds the core regulator output on VDDA_VCAP. RF1 leaves through a ladder of C13 to ground, L3 paralleled by C14, C11 to ground, L4, C12 to ground and the series DC block C10 to the antenna. A 32.768 kHz crystal with its two load capacitors sits on PB12 and PB13; a 32 MHz crystal sits on OSCIN and OSCOUT with no load capacitors. All six ground balls go to ground. RSTN and the GPIOs are left free.

parts.note: high-speed crystal (XTAL_HS); its two case pins go to ground

notes: For a board with the converter off, L1 is not fitted and the supply is wired to VFBSD.

circuits.title: Application circuit, DC-DC converter, VFQFPN32
circuits.description: The same system for the VFQFPN32 part. VDDSD (C5, C6), VDDRF (C3, C4), VDD2 (C1, C2) and VDD1 (C17) each take their decoupling from the one VDD supply. The converter path, the core capacitor C7, the RF matching ladder to the antenna and both crystals are wired as on the WLCSP36 circuit. Ground is VSSSD (pin 26) and the exposed pad (pin 33). RSTN and the GPIOs are left free.

parts.note: high-speed crystal (XTAL_HS); its two case pins go to ground

notes: For a board with the converter off, L1 is not fitted and the supply is wired to VFBSD.

circuits.title: RSTN pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from RSTN to ground filters parasitic resets, and a push-button from RSTN to ground gives a manual reset. The pull-up to VDD (RPU, 25 kΩ to 55 kΩ) is inside the chip, ahead of a Schmitt trigger and a filter. The capacitor goes right at the pin, and whatever drives RSTN must take it below VIL(RSTN) max for the reset to register.

circuits.title: Supply with the step-down converter
circuits.description: VDD and VDDSD both take the supply. An inductor runs from VLXSD to VFBSD, and a capacitor to ground on VFBSD completes the converter output, which feeds the main LDO and the RF LDO. A second capacitor to ground on VCAP holds the core regulator output.
notes: VDD1 stands for every VDD supply pin of the package.

circuits.title: Supply without the step-down converter
circuits.description: With the converter unused, VDD, VDDSD and VFBSD are all tied to the supply and VLXSD is left open; only the VCAP capacitor to ground is needed. This suits low supply voltages or designs where power use is not critical.
notes: VDD1 stands for every VDD supply pin of the package.

operation.text: A Bluetooth LE 5.4 system-on-chip built round a Cortex-M0+ at up to 64 MHz, with 512 KB of flash, 64 KB of SRAM in four 16 KB banks, 4 KB of PKA RAM, 1 KB of OTP and 7 KB of ROM. The same radio also runs proprietary 2.4 GHz protocols. It can run the application and the Bluetooth stack together on one chip, or serve as a network processor. Supply 1.7 V to 3.6 V; ambient -40 °C to +105 °C, junction to +125 °C.

Bluetooth 5.4 LE with 2 Mbit/s, coded PHY long range, advertising extensions, direction finding (AoA/AoD), isochronous streams (BIS and CIS), connection subrating, encrypted advertising, periodic advertising with responses, EATT and more. Sensitivity -97 dBm at 1 Mbit/s and -104 dBm at 125 kbit/s; output power programmable to +8 dBm at the antenna connector; up to 128 connections; PHY rates from 125 kbit/s through 500 kbit/s and 1 Mbit/s to 2 Mbit/s. Balun on chip; an external PA and LNA can be used. Aimed at ETSI EN 300 328, EN 300 440, FCC CFR47 part 15 and ARIB STD-T66.

12 nA in Shutdown at 1.8 V. In Deepstop at 1.8 V with RAM retained and the radio wakeup source: 0.9 µA with the LSE crystal, 1.2 µA with the internal LSI. Peak current 4.9 mA transmitting at 0 dBm and 3.6 mA receiving at sensitivity, both at 3.3 V. Dynamic current 14.47 µA/MHz.

Eight-channel DMA with DMAMUX; one SPI that can run I2S; one I2C (SMBus/PMBus, Fm+); one LPUART; one USART (ISO 7816 smart card, IrDA, SPI master, Modbus, LIN, RS485 driver enable); independent watchdog; RTC; SysTick; one 16-bit four-channel timer (TIM2) and two 16-bit two-channel timers (TIM16, TIM17) with an infrared output; quadrature decoder; 12-bit ADC with eight inputs; 20 GPIOs, all 5 V tolerant, all able to wake the chip and all holding their state in low-power modes.

Flash read and write protection; the SWD port can be disabled; secure bootloader; storage for Bluetooth keys; true random generator to NIST SP 800-90B, producing 128-bit values from nine free-running ring oscillators; AES-128 co-processor; public key accelerator for modular exponentiation up to 3136-bit moduli and ECC scalar multiplication, ECDSA sign and verify up to 521 bits, with constant-time operation; CRC unit; 64-bit unique ID.

The Cortex-M0+ has a two-stage pipeline, a single-cycle multiplier and runs from 1 MHz to 64 MHz. Its MPU covers up to eight regions sized from 32 bytes to the full 4 GB and can be bypassed. A 32-bit multilayer AHB matrix joins three masters (CPU, DMA, radio) to nine slaves (flash, the four SRAM banks, APB0, APB1, AHB0 and the radio bus on APB2). The NVIC takes 32 vectored interrupts at four priority levels, with NMI and VTOR. The DMA has eight channels, each tied to a hardware request or software trigger, with four software priority levels, byte, half-word or word transfers, circular buffers and up to 65536 items per transfer.

Flash is one 512 KB bank of 256 pages, 2 KB each, read and written 32 bits at a time, with single or 4 x 32-bit burst writes, page and mass erase, and write protection over four segments of variable size. The 7 KB ROM holds the UART bootloader in its first 6 KB and factory values such as ADC trims in its last 1 KB. The 1 KB OTP cannot be erased; writing its last word at 0x1000 1BFC and resetting locks it against further writes. Software can remap address 0x0000 0000 to flash or SRAM0 with the REMAP bit.

The on-chip SMPS steps VDD down to a programmable 1.2 V to 1.90 V, switching at 4 MHz or 8 MHz, and feeds the internal LDOs. It needs an external inductor and capacitor on VLXSD and VFBSD. When the supply is low or power is not critical it can be left out: VFBSD is then wired to VDD and no inductor is fitted.

Three domains: VDD33 (1.7 V to 3.6 V), which feeds part of the I/O ring, the regulators, power management and oscillators; VDD12o, always on, 1.2 V when active and 1.0 V in Deepstop; and VDD12i, 1.2 V when active and off in Deepstop. The main LDO makes 1.2 V from a 1.4 V to 3.3 V input for both digital domains while running. A low-power regulator at 1.0 V stays on all the time and takes over VDD12o in Deepstop. A separate RF LDO supplies 1.2 V to the radio.

Power-on reset holds the chip while VDDIO is below about 1.65 V. Power-down reset, always on, resets the chip when VDD falls about 20 mV under the POR threshold (1.58 V typical). The programmable voltage detector watches VDDIO against one of seven thresholds from 2.05 V to 2.91 V, or an external voltage on PWR_PVD_IN against about 1 V, and raises an interrupt when the level falls below.

PORESETn comes from POR and PDR, and from leaving Shutdown, and resets everything. The system reset PADRESETn adds the watchdog, a CPU lockup (masked while a debugger is attached), a software request through SYSRESETREQ in AIRCR, and the RSTN pin. It spares the debug logic, flash key management, the RTC timer, the power controller and part of the RCC. Internal sources produce a reset pulse of at least 20 µs, and RSTN is driven low to signal it; a reset from outside starts while RSTN is held low.
In Run everything can be active; clocks to unused peripherals can be gated off to save current. Idle keeps flash, clocks and supplies on with the CPU stopped.

Entered with the radio and CPU asleep (WFI with SLEEPDEEP), no unmasked wakeup source pending and LPMS = 0. Clocks stop and only the always-on domain stays up at 1.0 V. RAM0 is always kept; RAM1 to RAM3 are kept or dropped under software control. The low-speed clock can run from the LSE or LSI or be stopped; with it running, the RTC, IWDG, LPUART and the radio wakeup timer stay active. All 20 GPIOs keep their configuration and can hold a static output; PA10 can output the low-speed clock and PA8 the RTC output. Wakeup comes from the radio timer (radio or CPU host time reached), the RTC, an IWDG reset, the LPUART or any GPIO. On wakeup the switched-off logic is reset and the CPU reboots; the power controller records the cause. Wakeup to Run takes 170 µs typical from a GPIO at 3.3 V.

The lowest-current state, entered like Deepstop but with LPMS = 1. All regulators and clocks, including LSI and LSE, are off and only the VDDIO domain stays up; I/O pull-ups and pull-downs can be kept. The only ways out are a low pulse on RSTN or a configured pulse on PB0, and leaving behaves like a power-on reset. PDR may be on or off during Shutdown.

The system clock comes from the 64 MHz HSI RC, the 64 MHz PLL locked to the 32 MHz HSE crystal, or the HSE directly. HSI and PLL share one block, RC64MPLL, which is only accurate once the crystal runs and the PLL locks. After reset the system runs at 16 MHz (64 MHz divided by four). The low-speed tree, for the radio timers, RTC, IWDG and LPUART, runs from the LSI (a fixed frequency somewhere between 24 kHz and 49 kHz depending on the part), the LSE (a 32.768 kHz crystal or a single-ended clock) or a 32 kHz clock divided from HSI or HSE, which is lost in Deepstop. All low-speed sources are off after reset. Clocks can be brought out on RCC_LCO (low speed) and RCC_MCO (high speed).

I2C and USART always count baud rates from a fixed 16 MHz, and the LPUART from 16 MHz or the LSE, so the system clock can change during a transfer. The SPI uses the system clock except in I2S mode, where 16 MHz, 32 MHz or the system clock can be chosen. TRNG and the flash controller also use a fixed 16 MHz; the ADC uses 64 MHz divided to 16 MHz; the radio uses fixed 16 MHz and 32 MHz clocks besides a divided system clock for its bus interfaces.

A 32 MHz crystal specified for 6 pF to 8 pF of load. The chip carries its own load capacitance, a fixed part plus a 6-bit binary-weighted bank set by XOTUNE, with steps of about 0.07 pF; with a typical crystal pulling of -14 ppm/pF the frequency can be trimmed to about 1 ppm, which takes up board stray capacitance.

Transmit modulates the carrier directly; receive uses a low-IF chain with I/Q filtering and AGC at RF and IF. An internal transformer lets RF1 drive a single-ended antenna near 50 Ω, and its band-pass shape eases the external harmonic and blocking filter. Output power is set through the PA's programmable LDO, with a smoothed ramp. VSSRF pins, and on VFQFPN32 the exposed pad, go to the ground plane. A companion IPD, MLPF-NRG-01D3, is offered for matching and filtering.

RADIO_TX_SEQUENCE (PA10 AF2 or PB14 AF1) is high while the radio transmits and RADIO_RX_SEQUENCE (PA8 AF2 or PA11 AF2) while it receives, for driving an external antenna switch or for coexistence with other radios. RADIO_RF_ACTIVITY, on PB7, is the OR of the two and suits an antenna switch during AoA or AoD.

For AoA reception and AoD transmission the radio handles the constant tone extension and outputs a 7-bit antenna number, RADIO_ANTENNA_ID[6:0] (bit 0 least significant), on GPIO alternate functions to drive an external antenna switch during the CTE.

12-bit SAR converter at up to 1 Msps with input ranges of 0 V to 1.2 V, 2.4 V or 3.6 V. Up to eight single-ended inputs or four differential pairs or a mix, plus the temperature sensor and battery voltage up to 3.6 V. Single or continuous conversion, a down-sampler with ratios 1 to 128 that lifts resolution to 16 bits, an analog watchdog, DMA and interrupts. The temperature sensor is calibrated per part and its calibration is stored in system memory. When VBAT is below 2.7 V the analog switches rely on the I/O booster.

TIM2 has four channels for capture, compare, PWM or one-pulse, DMA and quadrature encoder input. TIM16 and TIM17 each have one channel plus a complementary output, 16-bit counter and prescaler, DMA, and together form the IR output. The IWDG is a 12-bit down-counter with an 8-bit prescaler on the low-speed clock and runs in Deepstop. SysTick is a 24-bit down-counter. The RTC keeps BCD time and calendar with leap-year handling, alarms, a periodic wakeup and 0.95 ppm digital calibration; it keeps running through low-power modes, resets and debugger halts while the supply is in range.

I2C: master and slave, Sm 100 kbit/s, Fm 400 kbit/s, Fm+ 1 Mbit/s, 7- and 10-bit addressing, SMBus 2.0 and PMBus 1.1, analog and digital filters, DMA. The SDA and SCL pins are not true open drain: the PMOS to VDD is switched off but present, and the Fm+ 20 mA drive is only partly met. USART: up to 2 Mbit/s with automatic baud detection, hardware flow control, DMA. LPUART: wakes the chip from Deepstop at up to 9600 baud on the 32.768 kHz LSE, on start bit, any frame or a set frame; faster in Run. SPI3: master or slave up to 32 Mbit/s, Motorola and TI modes, hardware CRC, DMA; its I2S mode does Philips, MSB, LSB and PCM formats, half duplex.

The ROM bootloader runs from reset when PA10 is held high during a hardware reset; otherwise the flash application starts. It detects baud rate up to 1 Mbit/s and can mass or section erase, program flash and set or clear readout protection.
Two-wire SWD on DEBUG_SWDIO (PA2) and DEBUG_SWCLK (PA3), with four breakpoints and two watchpoints.

Each pin can be a push-pull or open-drain output, an input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or an alternate function; the ports sit on AHB0 for fast toggling and the configuration can be locked. Pins are analog inputs during and after reset. Outputs drive ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL and VOH; total current through all I/Os plus the chip's own use stays within ΣIVDD and ΣIVGND.

Unless stated, limits hold at TA = 25 °C, VDD = 3.3 V, system clock 32 MHz from the HSI and SMPS at 4 MHz; values marked as characterised are mean ±3σ, and typical ADC figures are mean ±2σ over temperature. Pin parameters are measured with a 50 pF load to ground.

With the SMPS running, part of the power is lost in the external inductor rather than the chip, depending on the inductor's ESR. Radiated RF power is under 4 mW and need not be subtracted. RF figures are given up to 85 °C.
